clean_check: Read server/internal/auth/store.go, server/internal/handler/middleware.go, server/internal/handler/auth.go, server/internal/handler/http.go, server/cmd/main.go, server/cmd/main_test.go in full, plus tech-spec.md Decisions 1/2/6/7/8/10/17/19, user-spec.md, tasks/4.md, and decisions.md Tasks 1-3. Live-verified (not just read) against a running instance (go run ./cmd, MemoryRepository, real newMux) and against the full test suite run inside golang:1.25-alpine with --network host against poshivon_test (MariaDB 11.4, schema 001-005): `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` all clean; `go test ./... -count=1` all packages ok including cmd, internal/auth, internal/handler (0 skip/fail on the DB-backed store tests). Hunted: A01 (Broken Access Control) — confirmed RequireAccess/RequireAdmin route through AccessService.GetAccessState only (grepped internal/handler for any local `has_access ||`/`role ==` re-derivation — found none outside comments), confirmed RequireAuth fail-closed on NULL yandex_login live via curl-equivalent test suite and via reading ResolveSession/RequireAuth. A02 (Crypto) — refresh tokens hashed with SHA-256 before storage (pre-existing, unchanged). A03 (Injection) — read every query in store.go: 100% parameterized `?` placeholders, no string concatenation, no new injection surface. A04 (Insecure design) — Decision 8's Origin fallback-to-r.Host logic reviewed and matches spec exactly, verified live that empty allowlist does NOT bypass the check (confirmed via passing TestRequireSameOrigin_EmptyAllowlistFallsBackToHost and by reading originAllowed()). A05 (Misconfiguration) — no default-allow origin, no permissive CORS added by this task. A06 (Dependencies) — no new modules added (task uses only stdlib + existing deps, confirmed against tech-spec Dependencies section). A07 (Auth failures) — session identity fail-closed (Decision 2) verified live against real DB; new 401/403/502/500 slugs (`session_identity_missing`, `yandex_profile_failed`, `user_ensure_failed`) confirmed absent from client/src/utils/yandexAuth.js's shouldRefreshAuth retry allowlist by reading that file directly. A08 (Integrity) — no deserialization of untrusted data beyond existing JSON decode with DisallowUnknownFields (pre-existing). A09 (Logging) — confirmed writeAPIDomainError logs the original error server-side before responding (Decision 17), verified via passing TestWriteAPIDomainError_LogsOriginalError. A10 (SSRF) — no new user-controlled URLs reach outbound requests; YandexTokenURL/YandexUserInfoURL come only from config, not request input. Hardcoded-secrets scan: grepped all six task files for API_KEY=/SECRET=/PASSWORD=/TOKEN= literal-assignment patterns and base64-looking blobs — all matches were config-field references (cfg.YandexClientSecret, etc.), zero literal credential values.

verification_notes.decision_7_legacy_endpoint: Live-confirmed: `POST /auth/yandex` returns 404 against the actual `newMux()` the running server uses (curl against `go run ./cmd/.` on port 18080), not a hand-built test mux. Grepped the whole server tree for `HandleYandexLogin` and the literal route string `/auth/yandex"` — zero remaining references outside comments and test assertions (cmd/main_test.go:41, internal/handler/auth_test.go:740 both assert 404). No second registration, fallback route, or middleware short-circuit reintroduces the old flow.
verification_notes.decision_2_fail_closed_identity: Confirmed via full read of RequireAuth (middleware.go:47-72): a session with NULL/empty YandexLogin is rejected with 401 `session_identity_missing` before identity ever reaches context. Confirmed live: TestAuthStore_NullYandexLoginRoundTrips (real MariaDB, NULL round-trips without error) and TestRequireAuth_NullIdentitySession both pass in the live `go test ./internal/auth/... ./internal/handler/...` run. Read client/src/utils/yandexAuth.js:14-16 directly: shouldRefreshAuth's allowlist is exactly `["access_cookie_missing", "access_expired", "access_mismatch"]` — `session_identity_missing` is absent, so the client will not enter a retry loop it can't resolve; it must send the user to a fresh login as intended.
verification_notes.decision_8_origin_csrf_CRITICAL_CONTEXT: IMPORTANT, already self-flagged by the implementer in decisions.md and confirmed here by live testing: RequireSameOrigin/RequireAuth/RequireAccess/RequireAdmin are fully implemented and unit/integration-tested in isolation, but main.go's newMux() and main() do NOT wire ANY of them onto the real routes yet — this wiring is explicitly deferred to Task 5 (access.go, admin/access routes) and Task 6 (http.go, /api/v1/users/* conversion) per the tech-spec's route table and per this task's own 'What to do' item 6, which explicitly forbids touching route-chain assembly. Live-verified against the actual running server built from this exact code: `curl -X POST /auth/yandex/code -H 'Origin: http://evil.example'` was accepted through to the Yandex-exchange step (only failed because no real Yandex credentials were configured, not because of an Origin check) — i.e. login-CSRF protection is NOT active in the current build. `curl /api/v1/users/ivanov/chats` with zero cookies returned 200 `{"items":[]}` — the existing data routes remain completely open, exactly as they were before this feature, because http.go still reads userID from the URL segment (Task 6's job) and no RequireAuth/RequireAccess chain sits in front of APIHandler.Register in newMux(). This is consistent with, and does not violate, this task's declared scope (task file explicitly excludes route wiring in item 6 and lists it as Task 5/6 responsibility) — it is reported here as a critical fact for the orchestrator: this task's acceptance criteria are all met, but the feature as a whole is NOT security-effective until Task 5/6 land. If Task 5/6 are skipped, deferred, or the deploy pipeline ships this commit alone, /api/v1/users/*, /auth/yandex/code, /auth/refresh and /auth/logout are exploitable in production exactly as verified live above.
verification_notes.decision_10_no_reimplementation: Grepped internal/handler/*.go (excluding _test.go) for `has_access`, `HasAccess`, `RoleAdmin`, `role ==`: the only occurrences are middleware.go:106 (`state.HasAccess`, read from AccessService.GetAccessState's return value) and middleware.go:123 (`state.Role != service.RoleAdmin`). Read access.go: GetAccessState routes through the single unexported `hasEffectiveAccess` helper (has_access || role=='admin'). No second copy of Decision 10 exists in the handler package.
verification_notes.decision_17_no_error_leaks: Read all 8 branches of classifyDomainError (http.go:263-284): every branch returns a fixed string constant, never err.Error(). Live-triggered three real branches against the running server: unknown user's GET /settings -> 404 `{"error":"not_found"}` (no SQL/repo text); disabled DeepSeek market-feedback -> 503 with a fixed message (pre-existing writeAPIError path, not writeAPIDomainError, out of Decision 17's scope but still not leaking anything sensitive). The handler package's own test suite (TestWriteAPIDomainError_NoInternalTextInAnyBranch) exercises all 8 categories against a synthetic error string containing SQL/DSN/table-name fragments and asserts none of those fragments appear in the response body — this test passed in the live `go test` run. A companion test (TestWriteAPIDomainError_LogsOriginalError) confirms the original error text is still captured server-side via `log`, satisfying both halves of Decision 17.
verification_notes.new_error_codes_502_500: `yandex_profile_failed` (502) and `user_ensure_failed` (500) are both fixed string literals passed directly to writeError(w, status, code) in auth.go — neither interpolates the underlying error (the real fetchYandexProfile/EnsureUser error is only passed to log.Printf, never to the client). Confirmed both slugs are absent from yandexAuth.js's shouldRefreshAuth retry list by reading the file. Neither collides with the six pre-existing slugs (access_cookie_missing, refresh_cookie_missing, session_not_found, session_expired, access_expired, access_mismatch) that the client's retry logic depends on for stability.
verification_notes.sql_injection_surface: Read all queries in store.go (CreateSession, FindByRefreshHash, UpdateSessionTokens, RevokeByRefreshHash): 100% use `?` placeholders via database/sql's Exec/QueryRow, zero string concatenation or fmt.Sprintf into SQL text. No new injection surface introduced by this task.
verification_notes.collation_bypass_reintroduction: Grepped internal/auth, internal/handler, internal/service/access.go and cmd/main.go for strings.EqualFold/ToLower/ToUpper/Compare applied to login/identity values: the only matches are auth.go:566 (SameSite cookie attribute parsing, unrelated), cmd/main.go:137 (APP_STORAGE config value, unrelated), http.go:125 (the `hard` query-param boolean on chat-delete, unrelated), and http.go:275/277/279 (matching DeepSeek's own lower-cased error text, unrelated to identity). No login/identity comparison anywhere in this task's code performs Go-side case-folding that could bypass the utf8mb4_nopad_bin collation fixed in migration 005 — all identity lookups pass the login straight through to the repository's DB-level comparison (AccessService.GetAccessState -> UserRepository.GetUser(ctx, login), no normalization in between, consistent with access.go's own comment: 'Только проверка, без нормализации... молчаливая правка значения здесь разошлась бы с тем, что реально лежит в users.id').
